title: Placement test
_note: Original items. Each item has a level band (1-6, see levels.json) and a skill. Speaking is not tested until the local AI tools arrive (M3).

items.passage: Hi, I am Tom. I am ten years old. I have a dog.

items.audio_script: Good morning. My name is Sara and I live in a small house.

items.passage: The shop opens at nine and closes at six. On Sundays it is closed.
items.prompt: When can you NOT visit the shop?

items.audio_script: The train to the city leaves from platform four at half past three.

items.passage: Although the new library is further from the town centre, most students prefer it because it stays open until midnight and has quiet study rooms.
items.prompt: Why do most students prefer the new library?
options: It is closer to the centre
It has longer opening hours and quiet rooms
items.answer: It has longer opening hours and quiet rooms

items.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.

items.audio_script: I was going to study medicine, but after volunteering at a school I realised that teaching was what I really wanted to do.
items.prompt: What did the speaker decide to do?

items.passage: Remote work has reduced commuting time for many employees. However, some managers report that spontaneous collaboration has declined, which may slow down the development of new ideas.
items.prompt: What concern do some managers have?
options: Fewer unplanned conversations may slow innovation
items.answer: Fewer unplanned conversations may slow innovation

items.prompt: Choose the best word: The results were ___ with earlier studies.

items.audio_script: While the treatment was effective for most patients, researchers noted that its benefits were smaller among older adults, so further trials are needed for that group.
items.prompt: What do the researchers say is needed?

items.passage: The author contends that economic growth alone is an inadequate measure of national progress, since it disregards inequality, environmental degradation and the unpaid work that sustains households.
items.prompt: What is the author's main argument?
options: Growth should be the only measure of progress
Growth ignores important aspects of progress
items.answer: Growth ignores important aspects of progress

options: Hardly had we arrived when the meeting started.
Hardly we had arrived when the meeting started.
Hardly had we arrived than the meeting started.
items.answer: Hardly had we arrived when the meeting started.

items.audio_script: Critics of the policy argue that, far from encouraging innovation, the subsidies have mainly benefited established firms that would have invested anyway.
items.prompt: What do critics say about the subsidies?
options: They mostly helped companies that did not need them
They were too small to matter
items.answer: They mostly helped companies that did not need them

items.passage: Notwithstanding its methodological elegance, the study's reliance on self-reported data renders its conclusions about actual behaviour somewhat tentative.
items.prompt: What weakness of the study does the writer point out?
options: Participants' own reports may not match what they really do
items.answer: Participants' own reports may not match what they really do

items.prompt: Choose the most precise word: The committee's decision was ___, so it could not be challenged later.

items.audio_script: The archive's value lies less in any single document than in the way the collection, taken as a whole, reveals shifting attitudes over two centuries.
items.prompt: According to the speaker, why is the archive valuable?
options: One famous document is in it
The whole collection shows how attitudes changed
items.answer: The whole collection shows how attitudes changed
